DOpus

DOpus is MixOS's file manager: two panes side by side, each a folder tree, with a Places sidebar on the left and a Properties sidebar on the right. The name is a nod to Directory Opus on the Amiga, whose twin panes it keeps.

The window

  • Two panes. Each shows one folder as a tree with Name, Size and Modified columns; columns that do not fit are hidden, Modified first. One pane is active; Switch Pane (Tab) moves between them, and copy and move always go to the other pane. Drag the divider to change the split.
  • The path field at the top of each pane always shows where it is. Click it, type a path and press Enter to go there; ~ is your home, and a file path opens the folder that holds it.
  • The tree. A chevron or a double-click opens a folder in place; another collapses it. Double-click a file to open it in its default application.
  • Selecting. Click a row to select it, Ctrl-click to add or remove one, Shift-click for a range. The arrow keys, Home and End move the selection.
  • Sorting. Click a column header to sort by it, ascending first; click it again to reverse.
  • Places lists Home, the filesystem root and your Desktop, Documents, Downloads, Music, Pictures and Videos folders, where they exist, followed by your saved bookmarks (ordered {name, path} entries in the config). Its toggle sits left of the left pane's path field.
  • Properties shows the selected item: kind, size, dates, permissions, owner and path, under a preview of a file when one can be made. Its toggle sits right of the right pane's path field.
  • Previews (View › Previews, per pane, on by default) are thumbnails from the desktop's shared thumbnail cache, made by the thumbnailers installed on the system (the same ones GNOME and COSMIC use). A type with no thumbnailer keeps its icon. Files on network, FUSE and automounted filesystems (NFS, SMB, sshfs, ntfs-3g and the like) keep their icons too, unless remote_previews: true is set in the configuration (below). A file whose filesystem stops answering keeps its icon rather than holding up the previews of the others.
  • Icons show what a folder or file holds: your well-known folders have their own, and files are grouped by their MIME type (document, code, image, audio, video, archive, spreadsheet, presentation, font, disk image, program, shell script).
  • Drag and drop. Drag rows from one pane onto the other, or onto a folder in it, and choose Move Here, Copy Here or Cancel.
  • Right-click a row or a pane's background for the actions that apply there.

Deleting asks first, and naming a new folder or a rename is checked before anything happens. Copies, moves and deletes run in the background, and the status line says how they ended.

Menus and keys

The menus hold every action except moving the selection (the arrow keys, Home and End) and the quick theme keys (Ctrl+Alt+D for light or dark, Ctrl+Alt+1 to 6 for a scheme; View › Theme has the full choice). Help › Keyboard Shortcuts lists every key in force.

To change a key, set it in the desktop profile: the binding applies at once, and DOpus's defaults stay for every action you leave alone. For example, settings.apply with keymaps.dopus.nav.parent: ["Ctrl+U"] makes Ctrl+U the parent-folder key, an empty list leaves an action without a key, and a reset of keymaps.dopus restores the defaults. See key bindings are desktop settings.

What it remembers

The two panes' folders, sorting and hidden-files setting, which pane was active, the split, and the sidebars' state and widths are kept in config.conf.mix in DOpus's own directory (by default ~/.local/state/mixos/apps/dopus/config/). dopus --print-config shows the configuration it would use. One setting lives only there: remote_previews (default false) makes previews of files on network, FUSE and automounted filesystems too.

For agents

DOpus answers on the Bus as dopus (schema dopus.v1).

CommandArgumentsAnswer
dopus.ping, dopus.describe, dopus.infoliveness, the control surface, version and build
dopus.stateboth panes (path, sort, hidden files, previews, selection, rows, status) and the sidebars
dopus.openpaths (one per pane), or one path and panegoes there
dopus.executeid, optional params; params.pane is left, right or active (the default)runs one action
dopus.actionsevery action, its keys in force and whether it can run now
dopus.theme.setscheme, modethis window's look
dopus.showrestores, raises and focuses the window through compd: {shown, target}
dopus.quitcloses the window

Every action accepts local and mesh callers, including file.open, file.new-folder, file.rename, file.copy-other-pane, file.move-other-pane and file.delete. dopus.actions reports the same availability as the keyboard and menus: selection, an idle worker and valid arguments still matter.

Mail selection (dopus.execute {id:"file.mail"}) sends the current pane's selected file paths to Email. It is available for one or more regular files, including symlinks to files, and appears in the File and row context menus. It launches Email through the session launcher when needed. A new message opens with the files attached; if a compose is already open, the files join that message instead. Email keeps paths and reads the bytes at send time. The Bus task performs these calls without blocking the window. The status area and action reply report whether a message opened, files were added or Email refused; the reply's result contains added, count and message. Headless instances support this action on their selection too.

File actions keep the normal name prompts, destructive confirmations and drop choices. After dopus.execute {id:"file.new-folder"}, use dopus.ui.type {text:"Projects"} and dopus.ui.click {label:"OK"} to answer the focused prompt. For rename, select the old text first with dopus.ui.key {key:"A",modifiers:["ctrl"]}. Answer a delete confirmation with dopus.ui.click {label:"Yes"} or cancel with label:"No"; a drop dialog offers Move Here, Copy Here and Cancel. These are the existing drive commands acting on the same dialogs a person sees. There is no separate dialog-answer command. dopus.ui.tree gives the current accessible labels when using another language. Delete keeps its normal confirmation. Existing destinations refuse a collision; they are never silently overwritten.

The window is drivable like every MixOS app, including its menus: see driving an app (dopus.ui.*, dopus.window). The commands are registered in docs/docs/spec/bus/commands.conf.mix.

Each command run from a menu, a key, a sidebar button or an accepted dopus.execute is published on dopus.action.executed, with how it was reached (menu, shortcut, ui or bus; executed commands). A refused action is not published.

dopus --headless runs the core and the Bus port without a window, for tests: the same commands, minus those that need a window. It publishes its accepted dopus.execute runs on <service>.action.executed too. Headless instances cancel name prompts and confirmations because there is no window to answer them; copy and move still use the real filesystem worker.

dopus --choose-service is a separate process registered as files, without the twin-pane window or the dopus.* commands. It serves files.choose, files.choose.result, files.choose.cancel, files.choose.list and files.choose.accept (the typed Accept for agents), the toolkit drive commands as files.ui.* and files.window*, and discovery, under the file chooser contract. Every accepted request has a secondary native window with the file manager's Places (including saved bookmarks, read without writing the config), path bar and single pane. Save confirms existing names before returning URIs; the chooser never writes the chosen files. Escape, Cancel and window close cancel the request. The last accepted folder is remembered per claimed app, otherwise per caller, within the provider incarnation.

Drive uses the request id as viewport. It is required when several choosers are open. files.window.state includes the serialised chooser state: folder and selection URIs, typed name, filter, choices, sorting and lifecycle. Without a display, choose returns UNAVAILABLE. compd currently exposes no portal parent-identifier resolver: windows centre on the focused output and are raised when mapped. A parent-relative stacking relationship cannot currently be established through that interface. The component owns the files@.service session unit template; adding it does not enable or start a service.

Macro Bus commands

The shared macro Bus surface uses this process's catalogue and runner. Subscribe to <service>.macros.finished for completion, where service is the instance’s registered Bus name (for example term-1234 for a second Term instance). Commands keep the app’s canonical prefix, such as dopus.macros.run.

CommandArgumentsResult
dopus.macros.list{}Catalogue and diagnostics
dopus.macros.reload{}Catalogue and diagnostics
dopus.macros.run{id}Acceptance and run number
dopus.macros.status{}Current or last run
dopus.macros.output{}Retained output and dropped flag
dopus.macros.stop{}Whether termination was requested
dopus.macros.new{title}Create a user per-app macro; {id,title,path,scanned}, without opening an editor; scan failures add warning and preserve the file

Logging: --debug[=LEVEL] and live Bus controls are described in live application logging.
